about.title: Personal Injury Help in Temecula, California
about.longDescription: Temecula is home to about 112,000 people, and in 2025 — the most recent final reporting year — the city recorded 451 injury collisions. Those crashes left 631 people injured and took 8 lives. Public-record counts show the heaviest collision volumes along Winchester Road, the northbound side of I-15, Rancho California Road, and Margarita Road, with reports tending to peak on Fridays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m., right as the workweek winds down and the roads fill. Behind each of those numbers is someone trying to figure out what comes next: how to cover an emergency room visit, whether to return the insurer's call, how long the soreness will last. That is where we come in. We handle personal injury claims in Temecula and across Riverside County. Our team works on contingency, so you pay nothing unless there is a recovery. Reaching out costs you a few minutes, and you decide what happens after that. No pressure, no obligation — just a straightforward way to get your questions answered.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Temecula Claim

items.title: The clock is two years — or less
items.desc: California gives you two years from the injury to file most personal injury claims, but if a government entity is involved, the deadline can drop to six months. Getting in touch early keeps those options open.

items.title: Partly at fault? You can still recover
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible reduces what you can recover rather than wiping it out. Even a driver found mostly at fault may still have a claim.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, lost enjoyment, and emotional distress. Your claim is not boxed in by a statutory ceiling.

items.title: Nothing out of pocket
items.desc: We work on contingency, which means our fee comes only from a recovery. If there is no recovery, there is no fee.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Temecula?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, you have two years from the date you were hurt. If your claim involves a city, county, or state agency — say, a Riverside County vehicle or a road maintenance issue — you may have as little as six months to file a government claim. Because these deadlines differ, it helps to contact us soon after the injury.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Temecula?
items.answer: Public-record collision counts for 2025 show the highest volumes along Winchester Road, I-15 northbound, Rancho California Road, and Margarita Road. Reports also tend to peak on Fridays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m. These are simply counts of where and when collisions were reported, not judgments about any particular street.

items.question: What if the insurer says the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault. That means your share of responsibility reduces your recovery by that percentage but does not eliminate it. We can review the police report and evidence to challenge how fault was assigned.
